title: Speaking Part 2 — one pair of photos, one card
note: Eight photo pairs. The minute in three chunks — Similarities, Differences, Speculating — on the school frame. Default, Alternative 1 and Alternative 2 keep the frame and rotate the key expressions. Built by build-part2.py.
tip: One sentence of similarities, one of differences — then spend the rest of the minute speculating to answer the question.

sim.name: Similarities
sim.hint: one or two sentences: what the pictures share

dif.name: Differences
dif.ask: Now the difference — in one sentence.

a.name: Compare
a.hint: one reason, with a comparison: 'much more … than'
a.ask: Now give a reason — compare the two.

spe.name: Speculating
spe.hint: answer the question for each picture — guess, don't describe
spe.ask: Now speculate: answer the question for each picture.

tasks.question: Compare the two photographs and say what might be difficult for the people in these situations.

photos.title: Office Meeting
photos.brief: A group of colleagues in a meeting around an office table.

photos.title: Working in Café
photos.brief: Someone working alone on a laptop in a café.

turn.why: The school frame: 'I feel that in many ways…', 'While… the second…', 'Starting with the first picture, it looks as if…'. Every blank is yours to fill.

segs.t: I feel that in many ways the two pictures are similar. They both show people working.
marks: I feel that in many ways

segs.t: While the first picture shows colleagues in a meeting, the second picture shows someone working alone in a café.

wrong.t: Both pictures also show people using laptops.
wrong.why: That's another similarity. The differences sentence needs 'while', 'whereas' or 'by contrast'.

wrong.t: In the first picture there are some people. In the second picture there are some people too.
wrong.why: No contrast and nothing specific. Name the difference in one sentence.

segs.t: Starting with the first picture, it looks as if the meeting might be long and serious. The hardest part is probably agreeing on a decision, because everyone has different ideas. Some people might also feel nervous about speaking in front of their boss. On the other hand, the person in the café could be a student. Working there is likely to be more relaxing, but it might be difficult to concentrate with all the noise. And I believe that working like this is not only more distracting but also lonelier, because there's nobody to ask for help.

wrong.t: In the first picture there's a long table, some laptops and a big window.
wrong.why: Pure description. The examiner can see the pictures — say what you think is happening, and why.

wrong.t: The people in the meeting are definitely arguing about money.
wrong.why: Too certain. You can't know from a photo — 'might', 'could', 'it looks as if' keep it honest.

I suppose trying different things is the best part of travelling, so I'd happily do both.

phraseBank.heading: 1 · Similarities — opening
phraseBank.note: One or two sentences, then move on.
phrases: I feel that in many ways the two pictures are similar.
Both pictures show…

There are obvious similarities between the two photos.
The common theme in both pictures is…
What they have in common is that…

phraseBank.heading: 2 · Differences — opening
phraseBank.note: One sentence with a contrast word is enough.
phrases: While the first picture shows…, the second picture shows…
The first picture shows…; by contrast, the second picture shows…
Whereas the first image is…, the second is…
However, there are some clear differences.
On the other hand, the second picture is quite different.
The main difference is that…
One major contrast is…

phraseBank.heading: 2 · Differences — detail
phrases: Unlike the first picture, the second one…

phraseBank.heading: 3 · Speculating — the heart of your minute
phraseBank.note: Don't just describe — guess. This is where your best grammar shows.
phrases: Starting with the first picture, it looks as if…

It seems as though…
It is likely that…
I imagine that…
Probably… / Perhaps… / Maybe…
